questions.q: Why does Overlook need at least two environments for this Bicep template?
options: Azure requires at least two environments for every deployment
A dev environment is needed to try changes safely, separate from a prod environment holding real patient data
Bicep templates can only be deployed once
There is no real reason, it's just convention
questions.explain: Changes to this template and to later chapters' security/HA-DR settings need somewhere safe to try first, separate from the real patient data in prod.

questions.q: What specific guarantee does the @secure() decorator provide for sqlAdminPassword?
options: It encrypts the database automatically
The value is never written to deployment history, never logged, and never shown in deployment output — it must be supplied at deploy time, never hardcoded
It makes the parameter optional
It automatically rotates the password every 90 days
questions.explain: @secure() is a specific Bicep guarantee against the value ever being persisted or displayed anywhere in the deployment pipeline.

questions.q: What would go wrong if sqlAdminPassword were declared as `param sqlAdminPassword string = 'TempPass123'` instead?
options: Nothing — it would behave identically to @secure()
The plain-text default would sit in the file and in Azure's deployment history, exposing the production admin password to anyone with read access to either
The deployment would fail immediately
The database would not get created
questions.explain: A plain default is visible in the file and recorded in deployment history — exactly the exposure @secure() is designed to prevent.

questions.q: Why does `location` get a default value (`'eastus'`) while `sqlServerName` does not?
options: Defaults are never appropriate in Bicep
location genuinely doesn't vary between Overlook's dev and prod environments here, while the server name must differ so the two environments don't collide
location is a secret value
sqlServerName cannot technically have a default
questions.explain: A default is appropriate when a value really doesn't vary — location doesn't here, but the resource names must differ per environment.

questions.q: What is the actual difference between deploying Overlook's dev vs. prod environment with this parameterized template?
options: Two entirely separate Bicep files must be written and maintained
The resource definitions stay the same; only the parameter values supplied at deploy time (like sqlServerName) differ
The sku block must be rewritten for each environment
Dev and prod cannot both use the same template
questions.explain: One template, two sets of parameter values — that's the entire point of parameterizing for dev and prod.
